Jamie — appreciate the clear ask and timeline. We're in a good spot to be pragmatic here. High level proposal (attached as a short PDF and worksheet):

- Commit reset: allow a one-time reduction of current FY28 commit by 20% for the remaining term (effective on signing). This reduces the committed baseline and adjusts monthly invoices accordingly.
- Invoice offset: Redwood can provide a one-time credit equal to 50% of the retained commit value (not to exceed $150k) that will be applied as an invoice offset over the next 3 invoices. The offset is contingent on AuroraAI increasing committed capacity by a minimum of 15% within 90 days of the renewal effective date.
- Upsell pricing: incremental committed units added within the 90-day window will receive a 10% volume discount for the first 12 months.
- Reconciliation: we will true-up actuals at the end of the contract year with standard true-up terms; any overages vs commit are charged at the agreed overage rate.

Thanks for looping me in. Karthik — this is negotiable and I like the structure. A few refinements to keep approval velocity high and protect revenue:

- Change offset cadence to apply as a single invoice credit at signing up to the $120k cap (reduces administrative churn).
- Require written confirmation of the committed uplift (15% min) within 60 days (shorter window) instead of 90. - Add a milestone clause: 50% of the increased commit must be active within 30 days of the uplift confirmation to avoid partial clawback; this helps prevent artificially timing usage to capture incentives.
- Keep 10% discount on the incremental committed units for 12 months.

Operational asks: Ben, can you confirm whether applying the credit at signing will cause any revrec or billing timing issues? Legal, we'll keep the amendment tight: one short SOW addendum + Exhibit A with commit numbers and the invoice-credit mechanics. I'll prepare the DocuSign with the language highlighted.

Jamie — if that sounds acceptable I can send the DocuSign by EOD today and we can get Procurement to sign. If you prefer the credit stretched over multiple invoices, we can revisit — but single credit at signing should be easier for both teams.
